name: การเผาไหม้ของปัสสาวะ
preview_text: Burning urination is not just about bacteria - in TCM, the location and origin of the heat determine the treatment. Most acute cases respond to herbs and acupuncture within a few d...
categories: ["ปัญหาทางเดินปัสสาวะและกระเพาะปัสสาวะ"]
synonyms: ["Burning Sensation During Urination", "Burning Urination", "Burning Urnation", "Hot Urination", "Burning or stinging sensation during urination", "Burning or stinging pain during urination", "Burning sensation on urination", "Burning pain during urination", "Burning painful urination"]
conventional_description: In conventional medicine, a burning sensation during urination is most often a sign of a urinary tract infection (UTI), where bacteria irritate the lining of the bladder and urethra. It can also be caused by sexually transmitted infections, vaginal infections, or irritants like soaps. Diagnosis typically involves a urine dipstick test or culture to identify the specific bacteria, and treatment is usually a course of antibiotics.
conventional_treatments: Most UTIs are treated with a short course of oral antibiotics, such as nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Pain relief may include phenazopyridine, which numbs the urinary tract but does not treat the infection. For recurrent infections, long-term low-dose antibiotics or post-coital prophylaxis may be considered. If no infection is found, the focus shifts to bladder pain syndrome or other non-infectious causes.
tcm_understanding:
TCM sees the bladder as a reservoir that stores and excretes urine, governed by the Kidney’s qi transformation. When heat accumulates in the lower burner, it disturbs this function, causing burning, urgency, and pain. The heat can come from external damp-heat invasion - often from diet or hygiene - or from internal imbalances in other organ systems.
The source of heat matters. Damp-Heat in the Lower Burner is the most direct pattern, where greasy, spicy foods or poor hygiene create a swampy, hot environment. But heat can also travel from other organs: the Heart, which is connected to the Small Intestine, can transmit fire downward if emotional stress or excessive heat builds up (Heart Fire transmitting to the Small Intestine).
The Liver channel passes through the genital region, so when Liver Qi stagnates and turns to fire, Damp-Heat can pour down (Liver and Gallbladder Damp-Heat). Even a deficiency of Kidney Yin can fail to cool the lower body, allowing a low-grade empty heat to simmer in the bladder (Kidney Yin Deficiency with Empty-Heat).
This is why TCM treatment for urinary burning is never one-size-fits-all. A young person with a sudden, intense burning after a spicy meal needs a different approach than an older person with mild, chronic burning and night sweats. The accompanying symptoms - mouth sores, rib-side pain, low back ache - are the clues that reveal where the heat is coming from. The tongue and pulse then confirm the pattern.
classical_quote: 「热淋者，三焦有热，热气搏于肾，流入于胞，而成淋也。其状小便赤涩而痛。」
classical_translation: "Heat strangury occurs when there is heat in the Triple Burner, the heat contends with the Kidney and flows into the bladder, causing strangury. Its presentation is urination that is dark, hesitant, and painful."
classical_source:
Zhu Bing Yuan Hou Lun (Treatise on the Causes and Symptoms of Diseases)  ,  Volume 14, Lin Bing (Strangury Diseases) 									·
More references
tcm_diagnosis:
A practitioner starts by asking what the burning feels like and what comes with it. The most common culprit is Damp-Heat in the Lower Burner, where intense burning, scanty dark urine, and an urgent need to go point to a classic “Heat Strangury” picture. A yellow greasy tongue coating and a slippery rapid pulse confirm that dampness and heat are pooling in the bladder, often after spicy food, alcohol, or poor hygiene.
When burning urination shows up alongside mouth ulcers, irritability, and a deep thirst for cold drinks, the focus shifts upward. This is Heart Fire transmitting to the Small Intestine. The tongue tip will be especially red, and the pulse will feel rapid. The practitioner will ask about sleep, mood, and any tendency to canker sores to see if heart heat is driving the urinary discomfort.
If the person also complains of a bitter taste, rib-side fullness, and a short temper, the pattern is likely Liver and Gallbladder Damp-Heat. Stress and anger can stagnate Liver Qi, which then turns into fire and mixes with dampness, irritating the urinary passage. The tongue looks red with a yellow coat, and the pulse feels wiry and rapid - clues that point away from a purely bladder-based problem.
In more chronic cases, a mild but nagging burn, worse at night or after overwork, hints at Kidney Yin Deficiency with Empty-Heat Blazing. Here the body’s cooling reserves are low, so heat flares without the heavy, greasy signs of dampness. Night sweats, a dry mouth, and a red tongue with little coating, plus a thready rapid pulse, steer the diagnosis toward nourishing Yin rather than just clearing heat.

patterns.symptoms: ["Burning or stinging pain during urination", "Dark yellow, cloudy urine", "Heavy sensation in the legs and lower body", "Lower abdominal fullness and distension", "Yellow greasy tongue coating, especially at the root"]
patterns.worse_with: Spicy, fried, or greasy foods, Alcohol and coffee, Hot, humid weather, Prolonged sitting, Holding urine
patterns.better_with: Drinking plenty of water, Cooling foods and drinks, Rest and avoiding overexertion, Keeping the lower body clean and dry
patterns.why_this_happens: When Dampness and Heat combine and sink into the lower body, they settle in the bladder and urinary tract. The Heat creates a sharp burning or stinging sensation during urination, while the Dampness makes the urine dark, cloudy, and scanty. Together they irritate the bladder, causing frequent, urgent urges to urinate but only passing small amounts.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body, slightly swollen, with a thick yellow greasy coating that is thickest at the root. Pulse: slippery (滑 huá) and rapid (数 shuò), often more pronounced at the rear (Chi) position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Spicy, greasy foods and alcohol generate Dampness and Heat internally, which sink to the bladder and worsen burning. Drinking water and eating cooling, diuretic foods help flush out Damp-Heat. Rest conserves Qi, while overexertion and prolonged sitting can stagnate Qi and worsen Dampness. Keeping the area dry and clean prevents external Damp-Heat from invading.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Drink plenty of water to help flush the urinary tract. Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods, as well as alcohol and coffee, which can worsen Damp-Heat. Include cooling, diuretic foods like Job's tears (薏苡仁 yì yǐ rén), winter melon, and cucumber. Keep the genital area clean and dry, and avoid holding urine for long periods.

patterns.why_this_happens: When Liver Qi gets stuck - often from ongoing stress or frustration - it can smolder into heat and combine with Dampness. This Damp-Heat then spills downward along the Liver channel into the lower burner, irritating the bladder and urethra. That's what produces the sharp burning sensation during urination, along with the dark, scanty urine.

patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Anger and frustration stagnate Liver Qi, which then turns into fire and combines with Dampness - the very mechanism that sends heat down to the bladder. Greasy and spicy foods directly generate Damp-Heat, while alcohol adds fuel to the fire. Calming the Liver and choosing cooling, bland foods starves the Damp-Heat and allows the urinary tract to settle.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Cut back on alcohol and greasy, spicy, or deep-fried foods - these add Damp-Heat to an already overheated system. Eat more cooling, water-rich vegetables like celery, cucumber, and bitter gourd, and sip plain water throughout the day. Gentle exercise and stress management help keep Liver Qi moving so it doesn't stagnate and flare.

patterns.pattern_name: Heart Fire transmitting to the Small Intestine
patterns.symptoms: ["Mouth ulcers or sores on the tongue tip", "Burning or stinging sensation during urination", "Mental restlessness and irritability", "Feeling of heat in the chest", "Flushed face"]
patterns.worse_with: Emotional stress and anger, Spicy, fried, or hot foods, Overwork and lack of sleep
patterns.better_with: Cooling foods and drinks, Calm and quiet environment, Meditation or deep breathing
patterns.why_this_happens: In TCM, the Heart and Small Intestine are internally-externally related. When emotional stress, frustration, or excessive heat builds up as Heart Fire, it can transmit along the internal channel to the Small Intestine, which then passes the heat downward to the bladder. This is what produces the burning, stinging pain during urination, along with the classic signs of Heart Fire like mouth sores and mental restlessness.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with a redder, swollen tip and thin yellow coating; possible tongue sores. Pulse: rapid (Shu) and overflowing (Hong), especially forceful at the left Cun position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Heart Fire is directly aggravated by emotional upset and overheating foods, which fan the internal flames. Calming the mind and eating cooling foods help settle the Heart, while rest and relaxation prevent the fire from transmitting to the Small Intestine and bladder.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods, alcohol, and coffee, which add heat. Eat cooling foods like bitter melon, cucumber, watermelon, and chrysanthemum tea. Practice calming activities such as meditation or gentle yoga to soothe the mind and prevent Heart Fire from flaring.

patterns.pattern_name: Kidney Yin Deficiency With Empty-Heat Blazing
patterns.symptoms: ["Mild burning pain", "Scanty, dark urine", "Night sweats", "Five-palm heat (palms, soles, chest)", "Dry throat, especially at night", "Lower back soreness and weakness", "Mental restlessness and irritability", "Worse in the afternoon and evening"]
patterns.worse_with: Overwork and lack of sleep, Spicy, fried, or greasy foods, Emotional stress and anger, Hot weather
patterns.better_with: Rest and adequate sleep, Cool environment, Drinking plenty of water, Gentle exercise like tai chi
patterns.why_this_happens: When Kidney Yin is depleted, the cooling, moistening function of the lower burner fails. Without enough Yin to anchor the body's warmth, a low-grade 'empty heat' rises and settles in the bladder. This produces a mild burning sensation during urination, often with scanty, dark urine, and is typically worse in the afternoon or evening when Yin is naturally at its lowest.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red, thin, dry body with little or no coating (cracks may appear). Pulse: fine and rapid (细数, xì shuò).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Overwork and late nights directly deplete Kidney Yin, allowing empty heat to rise and irritate the bladder. Spicy and fried foods add external heat, making the burning worse. Rest and cooling, moistening foods help rebuild Yin and clear the low-grade heat, while gentle movement like tai chi supports Qi flow without draining Yin.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid spicy, fried, and overly heating foods that can further consume Yin. Include cooling, moistening foods like pear, silver ear fungus, black sesame, and tofu. Prioritize rest and avoid late nights to preserve Kidney Yin.

faqs.question: Can TCM treat a urinary tract infection without antibiotics?
faqs.answer: TCM can be very effective for mild to moderate UTIs, especially when caught early. Herbal formulas like Ba Zheng San have strong antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties. However, if you have a high fever, severe back pain, or blood in the urine, you need antibiotics immediately. TCM can then be used alongside to speed recovery and prevent recurrence.

faqs.question: How long does it take for the burning to go away with herbs?
faqs.answer: In acute cases, many people notice a significant reduction in burning within 24-48 hours of starting the right formula. Complete relief usually follows within a few days. For chronic or recurrent burning, the timeline is longer because the root imbalance must be corrected.

faqs.question: What foods should I avoid if I have burning urination?
faqs.answer: Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods, as well as alcohol and excessive coffee - these all generate heat and dampness. Sugar and dairy can also worsen dampness. Focus on cooling, water-rich foods like cucumber, watermelon, and celery.

faqs.question: Can acupuncture help with urinary burning?
faqs.answer: Yes. Acupuncture can quickly reduce inflammation and pain in the urinary tract by clearing heat and promoting urination. Points like Sanyinjiao (SP-6) and Zhongji (REN-3) are commonly used. It works well alongside herbs.

faqs.question: Is it safe to take Chinese herbs with my antibiotic?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, but always inform both your TCM practitioner and your doctor. Some herbs can interact with medications. For example, herbs that drain dampness may increase urination, which could affect the concentration of antibiotics. Your practitioner will adjust the formula accordingly.

faqs.question: Why do I keep getting burning urination even though my urine tests are negative?
faqs.answer: This is a classic TCM scenario. The infection may be gone, but the underlying damp-heat or yin deficiency remains, causing low-grade irritation. TCM can resolve this by addressing the constitutional imbalance, not just the bacteria.

faqs.question: Can stress really cause burning urination?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. In TCM, emotional stress stagnates Liver Qi, which can transform into heat and travel down the Liver channel to the bladder. This is why some people flare up during stressful periods, even without any infection. Acupuncture and stress-reducing herbs are key.

faqs.question: How can I prevent burning urination from coming back?
faqs.answer: TCM prevention focuses on strengthening the body's defenses. This might mean clearing lingering damp-heat with dietary changes, calming the mind to prevent Liver fire, or nourishing Kidney yin with herbs. Your practitioner will give you a plan tailored to your pattern.
